Agreed: today the Dafny file proves the model, the tests sample the code, and nothing ties the two together. Which validation do you want built for BE-033?

options.label: Model as oracle + mutation (Recommended)
options.description: Compile KernelProtocol.dfy to Python, as MemoryBackend.dfy already is. The kernel's real exits are then checked against the proved model, exhaustively over the whole finite space (routes, exits, runtimes, closable, posture) instead of by sampling. Then run the repo's mutation tooling (pytest-gremlins via run_mutate) on the protocol code to measure which code changes the tests actually catch. This ties model and code together and measures test strength. It adds one compiled oracle and a CI step; about M effort.

options.label: Exhaustive enumeration only
options.description: Replace the Hypothesis sampling with a generated suite over the full finite exit space, as test_condition_space.py does for other clauses. Every combination runs every time, and no Dafny build is involved. Stronger than sampling, but the model and the code are still not linked. About S effort.

options.label: TLA+ for close/run races
options.description: Model concurrent close against in-flight calls in sdd/formal/tla/ and run the TLC model checker on it. This is the only option that covers concurrency, which neither the tests nor Dafny touch. But the race belongs to the Session, which doesn't exist yet, so this is BK-455's scope. About M effort, and it delays this PR.

options.label: Keep PR, file item
options.description: Leave this PR as it is and file a backlog item for linking model and code. It records the gap, and the PR stays smaller.

questions.question: Round 5 hit the 5-finding-round ceiling with 4 findings. Continue the loop?

options.label: Fix all, round 6 (Recommended)
options.description: Fix the four findings test-first, then run round 6 as a verification and closing round (unprimed, measuring, whole-file). The findings are bounded and none came from a worsening fix pass. Expect one more round.

options.label: Fix, then stop
options.description: Fix the four findings and push without another review round. This breaks the stop rule, because the last fix pass would go unreviewed, and the Step 5 report would say so.

options.label: Stop here
options.description: File the four findings as backlog items and close with the PR as is. The spec keeps a false claim about read_bytes.

questions.question: How should read_bytes's condemned-stream close be handled?

options.label: Fix in this PR (Recommended)
options.description: read_bytes in both runtimes asks connection_dead on a stream failure and skips the close when it condemns the error, matching read. Cells are written red-first per runtime, plus read_bytes exits in the oracle suite. A small kernel change, and BE-033 stays true as written.

options.label: Narrow and file
options.description: Narrow BE-033, spec 006 and the guide to read, add a 'not yet met' row, and file a new BK item for read_bytes. No kernel change; the gap stays open on the common whole-file path.

questions.question: How should the model's admitted before-states be closed, now that the repeat-site check has fired?

options.label: Enumerate and pin (Recommended)
options.description: Tighten KernelExit's requires to the before-states the kernel can be in: a gate refusal opens nothing, and a caller-closed iterator counts as exhausted. Add one oracle cell that wraps the compiled KernelExit and asserts every before-state the suite passes satisfies those requires, so the domain stays equal to what the code reaches.

options.label: Narrow this edge only
options.description: Add the stream clause to GateRefused's requires and stop. This is what the repeat-site rule warns against: the next unreachable edge would be found by reading again.

questions.question: read_bytes closes a stream even when connection_dead condemned it, unlike read. This predates the PR, but the PR's spec text says the rule holds in both runtimes. How should this PR handle it?

options.label: Fix in this PR (Recommended)
options.description: Make `_io.read_all` take the verdict (skip `close_stream` when the driver condemns the error), test-first with a read_bytes cell per runtime, and add read_bytes exits to the oracle suite. Small, local, both runtimes via the generator; the spec text then becomes true as written.

options.label: Narrow and file
options.description: Narrow BE-033, spec 006 and the guide to `read`, add a *not yet met* row for read_bytes and file a backlog item. No behaviour change here; the gap stays open until that item lands.

questions.question: The repeat-site check fired on the model's admitted before-states. How should the precondition be closed?

options.label: Enumerate reachable (Recommended)
options.description: Close it once, by enumeration: a cell records every before-state the oracle suite drives (measured: 31), and a test asserts that every before-state the generator draws is one of them. Also add the GateRefused-stream requires. Any further unreachable edge then fails a test instead of being found by a reviewer.

options.label: Narrow this edge only
options.description: Add `exit == GateRefused ==> before.stream == SClosed` and stop there. Cheaper, but it is the third one-edge narrowing in a row, which is the pattern the repeat-site rule warns against.

options.label: Close after fixes

options.label: Keep looping

questions.question: How should the shift from recipes to declarative invariants be carried out?

options.label: ADR first, then BK-456 (Recommended)
options.description: Write an ADR on spec philosophy: postconditions and error precedence, not recipes; behavioural profiles (formalise hierarchical/flat); probe counts move to a per-profile cost section; a lemma governs where one exists. Then widen BK-456 to split spec 003 and prune each new file against that ADR. BK-449 closes as it is.

options.label: Also prune BE-033 now
options.description: Same ADR and BK-456 plan, and additionally prune BE-033 in this PR to ownership, transitions and cancellation only. Re-opens review on BE-033 in a PR already past its round ceiling.

options.label: BK-456 only, no ADR
options.description: Widen BK-456 to split and prune by the review's checklist without an ADR. Faster, but Rule 3 of sdd/000-process.md and the authority order stay as written, so the rewrite has no recorded basis.

questions.question: How far should the formal models become normative?

options.label: Lemma governs where it exists (Recommended)
options.description: Prose states each invariant in one sentence and links its lemma; where a lemma exists it is normative and the prose explains it. Rules with no lemma stay prose-normative. Extends Rule 7 rather than inverting Rule 3.

options.label: Models fully normative
options.description: Dafny and the Hypothesis state machines are the specification; prose is explanatory only. Needs an ADR superseding Rule 3, and every clause without a model loses its normative home until one is written.

options.label: Keep the current order
options.description: Prose stays normative, Rule 7 unchanged; only the recipe-style prose is pruned.
